title: closedStates: the object key and the engine's enforcement of it, released together (ADR-0162 item 1)
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ③ maintainer-directed · Source: ADR-0162 Execution item 1 (accepted by merge 972114df)

## 维护者速读

- 做什么：让应用在对象上写一行，声明哪些状态算「已关闭」（比如已付款、已审批通过），平台从此在每个入口拒绝对这类单据及其明细行的手工修改和删除。
- 用户会看到什么：已关闭的单据不能再改、不能删，明细行不能增、改、删、挪；提示语说明单据已关闭；系统自己的动作按钮和以系统身份运行的自动化不受限。
- 不做会怎样：需要冻结已决单据的应用只能继续各自写代码去拦，而且删除明细行这一种情况用代码也拦不住。
- 顺序：这张卡和审批相关的两张卡必须同一次发布，声明不能早于平台对它的执行上线。

## What happens

On `main` there is no way to declare that a document is closed. The platform unlocks a record when its approval is decided (`git grep -n "the record unlocks" origin/main -- content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`, two hits), and an app that needs a decided document frozen hand-codes it: the showcase carries three paid-invoice line guards in `examples/app-showcase/src/data/hooks/index.ts`. Removing a line cannot be guarded without code. `git grep -n closedStates origin/main -- packages ui examples content` returns nothing.

ADR-0162 (merged as `972114df`) decides the key and where it is enforced. The maintainer ruled the rule on 2026-11-22 (option C, ruling record 7073676422 on #32004) and the record's open points on 2026-11-26: 「全部按推荐」 (7200732942), 「平台堵住：撤回不恢复关闭值」 (7201405662) and 「平台拒绝这种配置」 (7205949718), all on #36253.

## Expected

The card has three slices. They ship in one release: the key is never published without its enforcement (ADR-0078, ADR-0162 D10).

**A. The key (D1).**
- `closedStates` at object level: a map from a field of the object to the list of that field's values that close a record.
- The field is a stored, single-value `select` field of the object. Each listed value is one of its declared options. A list is not empty and repeats nothing.
- A declaration that breaks one of those rules is a named refusal at parse and at publish. So is removing or retyping a field, or removing an option, that a declaration still names.
- Optional. An object without the key behaves as today. A line object declares nothing to be closed with its master, and may declare its own.
- No tie to a `state_machine` rule in either direction.
- The form row, the reference docs and the liveness ledger row with its runtime proof (ADR-0054).

**B. The engine's judgement (D2 to D7, D10).**
- Closed is read off the stored row: a record is closed when one named field holds one of its listed values. Nothing is stored for it, and there is no backfill.
- The unit is the record and every row that points at it through a `master_detail` field, one level deep. Lookups and satellite objects are not in it.
- A bound writer's update, delete, line create, line update, line delete and line move are refused as D4's table says. An update is judged by the keys it carries. A many-row write is refused whole before any row is written.
- A many-row write is judged by one existence probe asked of the store. A store that cannot run the line probe is answered from the one read of the matched rows that exists, under the engine's per-row ceiling. What cannot be judged is refused (D4 names the three cases).
- The lock is judged on the row as stored when the write reaches it, inside the write's unit of work. The write that closes a record lands whole.
- Who is bound (D5): every write not made in a system context, a write with no principal included. No grant opens a closed record. The state field is frozen with the rest. The pending lock's two passes do not carry over.
- Delete (D6): a bound writer's delete of a closed record is refused. A delete whose cascade would reach a closed record or a line of one is refused whole, where the cascade is planned and before the first row is removed. A system context deletes.
- Writes that are not a caller's change (D7): a referential clear lands, exactly the cleared field at the value the engine wrote. Restore puts an entry back as it stood, and refuses to put a row back under a live closed master that is not part of the entry. Change Owner and the hand-over of a banned user's work are bound and report each closed record among their failures.
- Placement (D10): after the object-permission and row-access gates, before the before-phase hooks. A master a write names is consulted only when the caller's own read door returns it. A master the stored row already hangs under is judged on its stored state, whoever the writer is. An object that neither declares the key nor is a line of one that does reads nothing extra.

**C. The refusal (D8).**
- One code, `409 RECORD_LOCKED`. The engine package becomes an emitter of it in the error-code ledger.
- Its own sentence family in the Operation Message Catalog, in every locale the catalog carries, with the four forms the pending lock's sentence has. The title is the one the writer would be served under its own field permissions, never the title as stored. The sentence carries no record id, API name or state value.
- The cascade's own sentence, in every locale: it names the record the caller asked to delete and the label of the object in the way, and nothing else.
- The upload-link door gains a closed-state sentence in every locale that door carries. Choosing between its two sentences by the lock read's reason lands with the lock-read card (item 2).

## Done when

- [ ] Slice A: the schema accepts the key, each authoring refusal has a test, and the form row, reference docs and liveness row with its runtime proof are in the diff.
- [ ] Slice B: every row of D4's table has a test for a record and for a line, for a single-row and a many-row write, on a store that runs the probe and on one that does not.
- [ ] The three "cannot be judged" cases of D4 are each refused, with a test.
- [ ] A write that closes a record and carries other fields lands whole. The next write is refused.
- [ ] A write with no principal is refused. A system context writes, deletes and restores.
- [ ] A delete whose cascade reaches a closed record removes no row, on a store with transactions and on one without.
- [ ] The engine-derived writes that reach a closed record are listed in the PR, each with the context it runs in and a test. One that turns out to run in the caller's context is reported to the seat and not exempted on the spot (D7).
- [ ] Whether a master that a before-phase hook supplies is judged is stated in the PR and pinned by a test. The reference gate treats only a caller-supplied value as the caller's (review note N14).
- [ ] Measured and reported: whether the approval status mirror's write and the request's finalisation share one unit of work (the first of the four readings under ADR-0162 "Execution").
- [ ] Verified and pinned: whether a customization overlay may add `closedStates` to an installed package's object, and that it may not shorten a package's own list. If the answer changes what a subscriber can do to a packaged document, it goes back to the seat as a decision card.
- [ ] Slice C: the ledger row, both sentence families and the upload-link sentence exist in every locale, and no refusal carries a title the writer may not be served.
- [ ] The key is authorable, so three things are named in the PR: the `skills/**` follow-up card, the docs (item 5), and an eval that exercises a declaration.
- [ ] The release carries items 7 and 8 with it (see Blocked-by).

Category ③: maintainer-directed. A build card of ADR-0162, child of #36253.
Grade: area:data · Feature · n/a (not a defect) · reach: every app that declares the key, none before · evidence: read (ADR-0162 Readings at `6c290d3af7`, premise re-read on `main` at `972114df`)
Suggested-grade: p2 · the grade of #36253, which the maintainer ruled; this card is the feature itself
Size: L (three packages: spec, the engine, the message catalog and its locales). Split along slices A, B and C before dispatch, on one trunk branch.
Business reason: carried from #36253. Apps that must freeze a decided document hand-code it today and cannot guard a line's removal at all.
Reader: seat 2 (repo:objectstack#2), one card thread per slice, effort high.
Release-order: #37766 (item 7) and #37767 (item 8) (release order: the key is not published before an approval is refused on a field that cannot show it, and before an abandoned or stranded approval can no longer leave a closed value behind). On a trunk branch this card's slices land first and the trunk merges last.
Clause-②: yes (widening). A new key on a published schema, a new emitter of a published code, new catalog entries. Nothing an existing app wrote is refused.
Metadata-protocol: added
Dedupe: searched `closedStates` (all issues): 1 hit, #36253 itself. Searched `"closed state" lock` (open issues): no other card on this mechanism.
Related: #36253, PR #37606 (ADR-0162), #24731 (the showcase guards), #35755 (the pending line lock).
